Subphenotyping and precision medicine approaches to ARDS.
articles.abstract: Sixty years after its initial description, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains defined by bilateral radiographic opacities and impaired oxygenation rather than by its underlying biology. This syndromic definition encompasses considerable clinical and biological heterogeneity, which may contribute to the ineffectiveness of pharmacotherapy trials to date. Subphenotyping aims to address this heterogeneity by identifying more homogeneous patient groups that differ in prognosis and/or treatment response. In this narrative review, framed by the research questions outlined in the 2023 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines, we synthesize current approaches to ARDS subphenotyping across complementary domains: clinical (etiology, rapidly improving ARDS), physiological (gas exchange, recruitability, elastance, and ventilatory ratio), morphological (focal versus non-focal radiological patterns), and biological (individual injury biomarkers and the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory subphenotypes). We examine their pathobiological basis, temporal dynamics, and retrospective evidence for heterogeneity of treatment effect, and consider how parsimonious biomarker panels, machine-learning classifiers, and adaptive basket trial designs may support clinical implementation. Prospective validation across diverse populations, including resource-limited settings, remains a key priority.

articles.title: Beyond the national average: Demographically stratified estimates of resource utilization for trauma systems planning.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Trauma systems are planned for populations, but resources are consumed by individual patients whose needs vary by age, sex, and injury pattern. To estimate the resources a population will need, existing tools often apply simple national averages of what admissions consume, creating a potential mismatch between the resources needed and those available. We compared simple population size-based estimates against estimates stratified by patient demographics. Using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Programs Participant Use Files (2022-2024), we conducted a retrospective analysis of adult admissions to 502 Level I/II trauma centers. Per-admission estimates for seven resources were derived from pooled 2022-2023 admissions using three approaches: simple estimates based on population size, singularly stratified estimates by age, sex, or payer alone, and jointly stratified estimates combining all three. Estimates were applied to held-out 2024 admissions and percent error calculated, with a 2017-2019 sensitivity analysis. Among 1,803,746 derivation and 947,281 validation admissions, the simple estimate fell outside 10% of observed utilization in 40 of 63 subgroup and metric combinations, 21 higher than observed and 19 lower. Blood product estimates were 236% higher than observed among Medicare-covered patients. Stratifying on one characteristic corrected error chiefly within its own subgroups (59 of 63 within 10%). Applied jointly, age, sex, and payer brought 62 of 63 combinations within 10%, reducing median absolute error from 13.8% to 3.0%. Simple estimates differed from observed resource use by 10% or more for nearly every patient group examined, failing in both directions in a manner no single adjustment can correct. Stratification by age, sex, and payer, characteristics knowable before injury, substantially reduced this error. Prognostic/Epidemiological; Level III.

Opioid administration prior to in-hospital cardiac arrest.
articles.abstract: Opioid administration is common in hospitalised patients. The opioid antagonist naloxone has been proposed as a potential adjunct during cardiopulmonary resuscitation. We aimed to describe opioid exposure within 24 hours before in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) and explore associations with outcomes. Retrospective observational study on all adult (≥18 years) IHCA during 2024 across nine hospitals in southernmost Sweden, registered in the Swedish Registry for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation. Opioid administrations were collected from medical records. Exploratory logistic regressions assessed associations between opioid exposure (any administration and cumulative dose) and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and 30-day survival, adjusted for age, sex, witnessed IHCA and national early warning score. Opioids were administered within 24 hours preceding IHCA in 108/267 (40%) patients and in 43/267 (16%) patients within the last two hours. Median time from last opioid administration to IHCA was 2.7 hours (IQR 0.5-7.7). Median oral cumulative morphine milligram equivalent dose was 17 mg (IQR 9-30). Naloxone was administered in 6/267 (2%) of IHCA. Opioid administration within 24 hours prior to IHCA was not associated with ROSC (OR 1.03 [95%CI 0.59-1.78, p=0.93]) or 30-day survival (OR 0.98 [95%CI 0.55-1.73], p=0.94). Higher cumulative opioid doses were associated with lower odds of ROSC (OR 0.91 [95%CI 0.83-1.00], p=0.042), but not 30-day survival (OR 0.98 [95%CI 0.90-1.08], p=0.69). Opioid administration within 24 hours preceding IHCA is common, with frequent administrations shortly before cardiac arrest. Further research is warranted investigating a potential role of opioid reversal during IHCA.

articles.title: MRI-Derived Spatial Patterns of Post-Cardiac Arrest Brain Injury Are Associated With Cerebral Oxygenation Dynamics.
articles.abstract: Post-cardiac arrest brain injury (PCABI) varies substantially in severity and anatomical distribution between patients. We evaluated whether anatomically resolved diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) lesion patterns are associated with cerebral oxygenation following cardiac arrest. We conducted a retrospective study of 24 patients with PCABI who underwent brain MRI and intraparenchymal neuromonitoring. Ischemic lesion burden was quantified as the percentage of tissue with an apparent diffusion coefficient <650×10-6 mm2/s across 164 brain segments. Principal component analysis (PCA) and k-means clustering were used to identify MRI-derived injury patterns for downstream physiological analysis. Brain tissue oxygen tension (PbtO2), intracranial pressure (ICP), and jugular venous oxygen saturation (SjvO2) were analyzed during the first 72 hours after cardiac arrest. Three reproducible MRI-derived injury patterns (i.e., clusters) were identified (n=13, 6, and 5), with progressively greater whole-brain lesion burden from Cluster 1 (10.16% [9.00-11.68]) to Cluster 2 (22.14% [17.83-25.12]) and Cluster 3 (38.40% [30.92-41.45]; p<0.001). Greater whole-brain lesion burden was associated with lower PbtO2 (r=-0.44, p=0.031) and higher SjvO2 (r=0.53, p=0.009), but not ICP (r=0.11, p=0.623). PbtO2 was lower in Cluster 3 than Cluster 1 (16.0±10.6 vs 26.6±9.0 mmHg; p=0.027), whereas SjvO2 was higher in Clusters 2 and 3 than Cluster 1 (both p<0.05). MRI-derived injury patterns differed in global lesion burden, PbtO2, and SjvO2, but not ICP. Greater whole-brain lesion burden was associated with lower PbtO2 and higher SjvO2, whereas no association was observed with ICP. These findings show that the extent and distribution of diffusion-restricted brain injury are linked to distinct cerebral oxygenation profiles after cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Reversed airflow during asynchronous volume controlled mechanical ventilation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: a physiological observational study.
articles.abstract: Chest compressions during the inspiratory phase of a ventilation can force air out of the lungs, so-called reversed airflow. Human data on this phenomenon during mechanical ventilation are lacking. We aimed to quantify its frequency and magnitude during asynchronous mechanical ventilation in intubated adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients receiving continuous chest compressions. This single-centre descriptive cross-sectional study used prospectively collected data from patients treated by a physician-staffed prehospital team. After tracheal intubation, patients were ventilated with an Oxylog 3000 transport ventilator in volume-controlled mode without positive end-expiratory pressure, during continuous manual chest compressions. Intratracheal pressures recorded via two catheters allowed calculation of airflow and ventilation parameters during the first minute after intubation. Reversed airflow was defined as expiratory airflow during the inspiratory phase of a mechanical breath. Continuous data are reported as median (first-third quartile). Twelve patients were included (median age 68 years [62-75]; 7 [58.3%] male), of whom 5 (41.7%) achieved sustained return of spontaneous circulation. Reversed airflow occurred in 10 (83.3%; 95% CI 55.2-95.3) patients and in 141 of 172 (82.0%; 95% CI 75.6-87.0) analysed ventilations. The median reversed-airflow volume was 61 mL [42-80] per episode. Median ventilation rate was 14 breaths/min [13-16], gross inspiratory tidal volume 324 mL [305-345], minute ventilation 4.8 L/min [3.8-5.9], and peak inspiratory pressure 46 cmH2O [40-52]. Reversed airflow occurred frequently during asynchronous volume-controlled mechanical ventilation with the Oxylog 3000 in intubated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients receiving continuous manual chest compressions. Its physiological and clinical implications require further investigation.

articles.title: Improvement in Peak Oxygen Consumption Following Cardiac Rehabilitation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest (OHCA) Survivors: A Comparative Study with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) Patients.
articles.abstract: To investigate the impact of phase II cardiac rehabilitation (CR) on cardiopulmonary fitness in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) survivors and to compare outcomes with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients categorized by Killip classification. This retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary medical center in Taiwan. We included 31 OHCA survivors whose cardiac events occurred between February 1, 2012, and June 30, 2023, and who completed phase II CR with symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) performed before and after CR. For comparison, 78 patients with STEMI were included, comprising 54 with Killip class I-II and 24 with Killip class III-IV. All participants underwent phase II CR, which was scheduled for 36 sessions and consisted of aerobic and resistance training. The primary outcomes were changes in CPET parameters after CR, including peak workload, peak oxygen consumption (V̇O2peak), and percent-predicted V̇O2peak. Paired t tests were used to evaluate within-group changes, and repeated-measures ANOVA was employed to compare between-group differences. OHCA survivors exhibited significant improvements in V̇O2peak (+3.9 mL/kg/min, p < 0.001), peak workload, and percent-predicted V̇O2peak after CR, with a mean improvement of 24.8% in V̇O2peak. These gains were comparable to those seen in STEMI patients across Killip classes. Although OHCA survivors had lower pre-CR V̇O2peak, they demonstrated similar trainability. This study highlights that OHCA survivors can undergo CR and achieve meaningful improvements in cardiopulmonary fitness, comparable to patients with myocardial infarction. These findings support the implementation of structured CR programs in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Delayed oxygen saturation recovery after the 6-minute walk test: Prognostic implications for COPD patients.
articles.abstract: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is a fundamental instrument in the clinical management of COPD patients, yet the prognostic value of specific physiological parameters during the recovery phase remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine whether the recovery time of oxygen saturation (SpO2-RT) following a 6MWT is associated with long-term prognosis (death and hospitalizations) in a cohort of patients with COPD. In this prospective observational cohort, 512 consecutive patients were recruited through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service and underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry, and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a ≥3% decrease in SpO2 from baseline during the 6MWT; SpO2-RT was the time from test completion until SpO2 returned to baseline. Of the 512 enrolled patients 25% were female. Those who experienced oxygen desaturation during the 6MWT exhibited significantly worse pulmonary function (FEV1%, RV%, IC/TLC and DLCO%) (p <.0001), higher fibrinogen levels (p =.01), lower quadriceps strength (p =.02), reduced PA (p <.0001), and a shorter distance walked (p <.0001). Within the desaturation sub-cohort, differences were analysed based on a SpO2-RT cut-off ≥ 80 seconds. Patients with a prolonged SpO2-RT exhibited more severe pulmonary function impairment (p values ranging from .02 to <.0001), significantly lower PA (p =.001), and shorter distance 6MWT (p <.0001). During the 3-year follow-up increased SpO2-RT was associated with increased mortality (p =.03) and hospitalizations (p =.0003). In the adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO2-RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalization (p = .02) and mortality (p =.04). A prolonged SpO2-RT ≥ 80 identifies a COPD phenotype characterized by diminished respiratory reserve and an increased risk of subsequent exacerbation-related hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. SpO2-RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.

articles.title: Respiratory Therapists' Intentions to Leave their Current Position.
articles.abstract: Many respiratory therapy departments face staffing shortages with high turnover rates. What drives turnover among respiratory therapists (RTs) is unclear. What variables are associated with RT's intention to leave their current position. We performed a planned secondary analysis of a multicenter, multinational study of RT burnout. We compared those with an intent to leave score ≥ 50 to those with a score < 50 and report odds ratios OR with 95% confidence intervals (CI) using univariable logistic regression. We received 1,014 responses and 536 (53%) had an intention to leave score ≥ 50. Statistically significant factors associated with intention to leave included: emotional exhaustion (OR 13.2), felt other RTs were burned out (OR 6.4), felt their workload was too high (OR 3.9), exposure to incivility (OR 3.4), unable to complete all their work (OR 2.4), inadequate staffing (OR 2.3), activities restricted due to illness (OR 2.0), worked 31-50 hours in the ICU (OR 1.6), bachelor's degree (OR 1.4) and missed work for any reason (OR 1.4). Statistically significant factors associated with low intention to leave included: felt valued by their organization (OR 0.1), a positive leadership score (OR 0.2), agreed their director/manager cared about them as a person (OR 0.2), satisfaction with total compensation (OR 0.3), < 2 years as an RT (OR 0.4), and spending their time performing high value activities (OR 0.6). Over half of RTs had an intention to leave. Emotional exhaustion, incivility, leadership, staffing, workload, hours worked in the ICU, bachelor's degree, and perceived value were all associated with intent to leave while hours worked, and patient population were not associated with intent to leave.

articles.title: Loss of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 activity during liquid plasma storage is associated with increased fibrinolysis in response to tissue plasminogen activator.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: In trauma, hyperfibrinolysis influences the need for massive transfusion and mortality. Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) sensitivity increases during whole blood storage despite rising plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) activity. Liquid plasma demonstrates preserved fibrinogen function in storage, but fibrinolytic regulation in stored liquid plasma remains undescribed. Liquid plasma tails (n = 28) were obtained and stored at 4 °C. Thromboelastography was challenged with 75 ng/mL exogenous tPA at three storage time points (day 1-3, 7-10, and 28) to assess resistance to fibrinolysis. PAI-1 activity was measured through a modified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) that captures only active PAI-1 utilizing immobilized active urokinase. Statistical analysis included two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Spearman correlation. Significance was set at p <0.05. Aging liquid plasma units demonstrated a significant, progressive increase in fibrinolysis (LY30) in response to tPA over time (p = 0.008). Alpha angle gradually increased, and maximum amplitude remained stable with storage. PAI-1 activity decreased with storage (p < 0.001) and inversely correlated with tPA-thromboelastography LY30 (Spearman r = -0.40, p = 0.04). Stored liquid plasma demonstrates declining PAI-1 activity, increased tPA-mediated fibrinolysis, and preserved clot strength, highlighting differences in fibrinolytic regulation compared with previously reported findings in stored whole blood. Further investigation into fibrinolytic regulation for the spectrum of blood products during storage and the implications for trauma resuscitation is warranted. Basic Science.

articles.title: Epigenetic Aging and Severity of Nocturnal Intermittent Hypoxia.
articles.abstract: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns. Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging? We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used. A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks. Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.

articles.title: DHEA-S in Pulmonary Hypertension: Insights from PVDOMICS.
articles.abstract: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status. Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status? We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH. DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p<0.01 for all). Associations between DHEA-S levels and PH severity metrics appeared most prominent in females with Group 1 PH. A doubling of DHEA-S was associated with a 2.8 mmHg (95% CI 1.6-4.1) lower mean pulmonary artery pressure, 3.2% (95% CI 2.0-4.4%) higher RV ejection fraction, and 22m (95% CI 11-33) farther 6MWD (all p<0.01). Higher DHEA-S associated with better RV function, but not pulmonary hemodynamics or 6MWD in females with Group 2 PH and males with Group 3 PH. In Group 1 PH, associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity appeared stronger in post-menopausal compared with premenopausal females. Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.

articles.title: Evaluation of the ACS Trauma Quality Improvement Program benchmark for intracranial pressure monitoring across trauma centers.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: In severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI), intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring detects and directs management for intracranial hypertension. ICP monitoring is recommended for sTBI patients and is included as a benchmarked quality metric by the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Programs (ACS-TQIP), which reports annual ICP monitor usage across all participating trauma centers. We evaluated whether greater institutional ICP utilization was associated with lower center-level mortality. For this retrospective observational study, adult patients aged 18 years and older meeting the ACS-TQIP definition of sTBI admitted to Level I or II trauma centers from 2013 to 2023 were identified. Patient data were aggregated by trauma center and calendar year to mirror the ACS-TQIP benchmarking framework. Annual institutional ICP monitor utilization and in-hospital mortality rates were calculated for each center-year combination. Multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models evaluated whether centers with higher ICP monitor utilization had lower mortality after adjusting for patient demographics, injury severity, neurological status, operative intervention, injury mechanism, and hospital length of stay. Among 191,686 sTBI patients, 29,224 (15.2%) underwent ICP monitoring. ICP monitor utilization ranged from 11% to 21% during the study period with a notable increase in 2017, whereas overall mortality remained largely unchanged. Year-specific analyses demonstrated a protective association between greater ICP monitor utilization and mortality in 2015 and an association with increased mortality in 2023. After adjustment for differences in patient and institutional characteristics, higher institutional ICP monitor utilization was not associated with lower center-level mortality (odds ratio=0.99, 95% CI=0.97-1.00; P=0.128). Using over a decade of TQIP data, greater institutional ICP monitor utilization was not associated with lower mortality across ACS-TQIP centers. These findings suggest that greater institutional adoption of ICP monitoring alone may not improve center-level outcomes and support periodic reassessment of ICP monitoring as a benchmarked ACS-TQIP quality metric. Level IV, prognostic & epidemiological.

articles.title: Secondary traumatic stress: A threat to surgeons and the patients they serve.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Secondary traumatic stress (STS) can present with symptoms nearly identical to post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, instead of resulting from direct exposure to trauma as the victim, STS develops after repeated indirect exposure to severe injury, death, and human suffering. This can cause significant psychological distress and ultimately contribute to PTSD-like symptoms and burnout. Evidence suggests that STS is common among trauma surgeons, although its prevalence remains poorly characterized. STS should be considered an occupational hazard of trauma surgery rather than a failure of individual determination or resilience and may have important consequences for the surgical workforce and, ultimately, patient care. We argue that institutions should consider a framework that incorporates monitoring of measurable workload and trauma-related risk factors at the individual surgeon level. These factors could prompt preventive measures such as protected recovery time and confidential screening using validated tools. When psychological injury is identified, surgeons should be afforded rapid access to mental health resources and formal peer support. Existing institutional programs demonstrate that these interventions can be operationalized, but their effectiveness in preventing, identifying, and treating STS requires further study. Addressing STS must be taken seriously as an institutional responsibility if we are to protect the trauma surgery workforce while supporting the quality and sustainability of patient care.

articles.title: Is the H-index an adequate measure of trauma surgeon research productivity?
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: The H-index is a widely used objective metric by academia to make critical decisions such as grant funding, hiring, promotion, and retention. The H-index is defined as the largest number (h) of publications that have received at least h citations. Unfortunately, the H-index presents many limitations including its inherent cumulative nature, incompatibility among specialties, its potential opaqueness to landmark research, and gender disparity among other potential threats to its validity. Alternatives to H-index that potentially address some of its core weaknesses are the relative citation ratio (RCR), fractional H-index, and the altmetric-index. The altmetric-index measures social and internet engagement rather than citations but has the advantage over H-index in providing more immediate feedback on a paper potential impact, especially among the general public. Trauma surgeons rank in the mid-to-low median H-index, driven primarily by low H-index among young faculty. H-index has value as an objective measure of research productivity, but stakeholders must understand its limitations, and it should only be used as one component of the total holistic assessment of an individual contribution to an academic surgical department.

articles.title: Infectious complications are preceded by specific longitudinal neutrophil cell surface patterns after polytrauma: Preliminary results of a prospective analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Alterations in neutrophil receptors provide valuable insights into the immune response after polytrauma. Point-of-care (POC) technologies enable rapid on-site analysis of neutrophils. Previous studies demonstrated individual neutrophil surface patterns after trauma, depending on injury severity and metabolic status. We hypothesized that infectious complications after polytrauma are preceded by specific neutrophil cell surface receptor alterations. A POC neutrophil analysis system (AQUIOS® Flow Cytometer) was implemented at a Level 1 trauma center. Polytrauma patients with an Injury Severity Score (ISS)≥25 were prospectively included. Neutrophil cell surface expression of CD10, CD11b, CD64, CD62L, and CD16 was analyzed immediately after admission and after 8 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 5 days. Patients were grouped according to the occurrence or absence of infectious complications. Thirty-two polytrauma patients with a median ISS of 34.5 were included in this study. Trauma sequelae included spine fractures, long bone fractures, and traumatic brain injury. During hospitalization, 13 out of 32 patients developed infectious complications. Patients who subsequently developed infectious complications showed significantly higher CD64 expression throughout the observation period, and CD62L demonstrated a trend toward higher expression. In addition, CD11b expression was elevated 8 hours after trauma. Longitudinal assessment of multiple selected neutrophil markers draws an individual neutrophil surface profile, with specific patterns associated with the development of infectious complications. This offers a promising tool for early risk stratification and identification of trauma patients vulnerable to post-traumatic infectious complications and allows for future immune-protective trauma surgery. Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Hospital volume and outcomes in after-hours emergency general surgery: a nationwide retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: High-volume hospitals are associated with better outcomes in some surgical fields, including emergency general surgery (EGS). However, the association of hospital volume with outcomes in after-hours EGS remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between hospital-year volume of after-hours EGS and in-hospital mortality and total healthcare costs. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database. We included patients aged ≥16 years who were directly admitted from outpatient settings and underwent after-hours EGS on or the day after admission between April 2014 and March 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; the secondary outcome was total healthcare costs during hospitalization. Associations were evaluated using mixed-effects models. Hospital-year volume was analyzed continuously using natural cubic splines and categorically (1-19, 20-49, 50-99, and ≥100 cases/year). Overall, 235,465 patients were included. In the mixed-effects logistic regression model, each 10-case increase in hospital-year volume was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.96-0.98; p<0.001). Spline analyses showed that the adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality generally decreased with increasing hospital-year volume, although this decline became less pronounced at higher-volume levels. Adjusted healthcare costs decreased across most of the volume range before increasing slightly at the highest levels. Compared with 1 to 19 cases/year, the aORs for in-hospital mortality were 0.77 (95% CI, 0.71-0.83), 0.72 (95% CI, 0.66-0.78), and 0.66 (95% CI, 0.59-0.74) for 20-49, 50-99, and ≥100 cases/year, respectively (all p<0.001). The corresponding adjusted relative costs were 0.99 (95% CI, 0.99-1.00; p=0.205), 0.98 (95% CI, 0.97-0.99; p=0.001), and 0.97 (95% CI, 0.96-0.99; p<0.001). Higher hospital-year after-hours EGS volume was associated with lower in-hospital mortality and modestly lower healthcare costs. These associations varied across the volume range. Prognostic/epidemiological; Level III.

articles.title: Clinical Features and Outcomes of Adenovirus Infections in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Multicenter Case-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract: Human adenovirus (HAdV) infection can lead to severe organ involvement in the ICU, particularly among immunocompromised patients. In this study of ICU patients with HAdV infection, we aimed to 1) determine the prevalence of HAdV disease, 2) identify risk factors for HAdV disease, and 3) evaluate its association with ICU mortality. Retrospective, multicenter, and propensity score case-matched study. Eight ICUs in France. Adult ICU patients admitted between January 2011 and January 2024 with at least one positive HAdV polymerase chain reaction result from any biological sample were included. HAdV infections were classified as either localized infections or systemic HAdV disease. None. A total of 169 patients were analyzed, including 115 patients (68%) classified as localized HAdV infection and 54 patients (32%) as HAdV disease. Hematologic malignancies were significantly more frequent in patients with HAdV disease (74% vs. 37%; p < 0.001). Twenty-three patients (43%) with HAdV disease received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Pneumonia was the main end-organ manifestation (n = 36/54; 67%). By multivariate analysis, allogeneic HSCT (odds ratio [OR], 3.04) and corticosteroid therapy (OR, 2.89) were independently associated with HAdV disease. ICU mortality was 45% (n = 76). By multivariate analysis, HAdV disease (OR, 3.15), performance status greater than or equal to 2 (OR, 3.35), and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores at admission (OR, 1.17 per point) were independently associated with ICU mortality. Mortality remained significantly higher in the HAdV disease group (OR, 10.50) compared with matched ICU patients without HAdV infection. HAdV disease occurred in approximately one-third of ICU patients with HAdV infection, predominantly among those with hematologic malignancies or corticosteroid therapy, and was independently associated with mortality.

articles.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation modulates immunosuppressive cells and IgA secretion in a gut microbiota depletion model.
articles.abstract: The relationship between gut dysbiosis and host immune dynamics remains poorly understood. We used an antibiotic-induced gut microbiota depletion model following fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) via co-housing. Mice received an antibiotic cocktail for 4 weeks (Abx group), or for 2 weeks, followed by co-housing with healthy control mice for 2 weeks (CoA group), or kept under conventional housing for 2 weeks (Abx-CH group). The gut microbiota was assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing and Gram staining. Immune cell populations were analyzed via flow cytometry using antibodies for T cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), IgA-secreting cells, PD-1+ cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in the colon and blood. As a result, α- and β-diversity differed from Control in the Abx and Abx-CH groups, whereas the CoA group resembled Control. Three distinct enterotypes were identified with a recovery pattern (Lactobacillus), a pathobiome pattern (Klebsiella, Escherichia, Proteus), and an expanded pattern (Ruminococcus and Prevotella) through FMT. In the colon, the proportions of Tregs were significantly higher in Abx and CoA groups. IL-10⁺ Tregs tended to increase in the Abx and were significantly lower in the CoA group. IgA-secreting cells and fecal IgA levels in the CoA group were significantly higher than in the Abx group, respectively (6.1% vs. 0.5%, 427.0 vs. 83.7 μg/mL, CoA vs. Abx; p<0.05). In conclusion, FMT could influence the proportion of immune cells in response to gut microbiota modulation. IgA secretion could be upregulated by gut microbiota after FMT.

articles.title: Reconsidering futility after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Impact of Steroid-sparing Immunosuppressants on Lung Function and Mortality in Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Evidence supporting steroid-sparing immunosuppressants (SSIs) in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (f-HP) remains limited. Do SSIs improve lung function or survival in adults with f-HP? Following Cochrane and PRISMA 2020 guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261413825), we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through May 2026 for studies of mycophenolate, azathioprine, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, or cyclophosphamide. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised studies using ROBINS-I, JBI, or Newcastle-Ottawa tools. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models pooled percent-predicted FVC and DLCO changes and hazard ratios for death or lung transplantation. GRADE assessed certainty. Seventeen studies (1,341 patients) were included. SSIs were associated with modest FVC stabilization (13 studies; +1.11% predicted, 95% CI 0.37-1.84; I2=0%) and DLCO stabilization (9 studies; +3.73% predicted, 95% CI 2.56-4.90; I2=24%). The estimand-consistent mortality pool of two adjusted overall-effect studies demonstrated no survival benefit and could not exclude harm (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.86-2.26; I2=0%). Certainty was low for lung function and very low for mortality. Descriptive benefit was concentrated in patients with identifiable antigens and less radiologic fibrosis. Modest lung-function stabilization largely reflects uncontrolled within-group changes, not definitive disease modification. Controlled survival evidence remains insufficient; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Ready for the Airway: Building and Sustaining Pediatric Airway Competence in Emergency Physicians.
An overlooked cause of refractory shock after liver transplantation.
Why is my patient hyperinflated?
Prediction of Acetaminophen-Induced Hepatotoxicity in Acetylcysteine-Treated Patients Using Routine Admission Biomarkers.
articles.abstract: Some acetaminophen-overdose patients develop hepatotoxicity despite acetylcysteine treatment. Established tools struggle to prospectively identify subsequent toxicity. We developed a model using only routine admission biomarkers to identify acetylcysteine-treated patients at highest risk and compared it with the current benchmark, the acetaminophen-aminotransferase multiplication product (AT product). Retrospective cohort study of acetaminophen overdose admissions aged 12 years and older (International Classification of Diseases 10th revision code of T39.1) with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤1,000 U/L at admission from 3 UK hospitals (2008-2024). We fitted elastic-net logistic models stratified by presentation ALT. The outcome was peak ALT >1,000 U/L. Performance was assessed on a 25% held-out test set and benchmarked against the AT product >1,500. Of 4,705 admissions, 119 (2.5%) developed hepatotoxicity. The model used 7 routine blood tests, 4 per stratum. At presentation, those with ALT ≤50 U/L, acetaminophen, sodium, potassium, and lymphocyte count remained in the model. In those with ALT 51 to 1,000 U/L at presentation, ALT, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and lymphocyte count were used. In the test set (n=1,175), it achieved an area under the curve of 0.93 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89 to 0.97) versus 0.82 (0.72 to 0.91) for the AT product (paired difference 0.11; 95% CI 0.01 to 0.22; P=.03), with higher specificity and a higher positive likelihood ratio at every matched sensitivity. The model had a specificity of 82.5%, whereas an AT product > 1,500 had a specificity of 62.6%. The model positive likelihood ratio was 5.1 versus 2.4 for the AT product, with half the number of false-positive escalations (171 versus 365 per 1,000 patients). A stratified model using only routine admission biomarkers (the Edinburgh Risk Score) identifies acetylcysteine-treated patients at the highest residual hepatotoxicity risk, outperforming the AT product >1,500 across decision thresholds, supporting selection for intensified therapy.

articles.title: Higher Quality Temperature Control Is Associated With Improved Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Multicenter Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Hypothermic temperature control has not consistently demonstrated a neuroprotective effect, resulting in heterogeneity of use in clinical practice. We evaluated temperature control quality across 4 institutions and its association with clinical outcomes. Retrospective analysis of institutional registry data collected between 2021 and 2024 in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with Glasgow Coma Scale Motor score less than 6 from 4 academic centers with established cardiac arrest programs. Eligible patients included those 18 years of age or older, treated with hypothermic temperature control (33-36°C) using a feedback-controlled device, and admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU). A temperature control quality score (0-6) was assigned for each patient. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge. The secondary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) score of 1-2. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions quantified the relationship between quality of temperature control, as an ordinal variable, and outcomes. Among 356 included patients, most were male (N=224, 62.9%) with mean (standard deviation [SD]) age 58.1 (15.2) years. Most suffered a nonshockable arrest (N=262, 73.6%) and did not receive layperson CPR (N=225, 63.2%). Median [IQR] Pittsburgh Cardiac Arrest Category score was 4 [3,4], mean (SD) lactate 9.1 (4.1) mmol/L, and pH 7.09 (0.17). Median [IQR] preinduction time was 2.3 [1.5 to 3.5] hours and 150 (42.1%) were treated with early neuromuscular blockade. Adjusting for confounders in the multivariable model, an increase of one-point in the temperature control quality score was associated with improved survival at hospital discharge (odds ratio [OR] 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 1.64). A one-point increase in the quality score also resulted in a shift towards lower (improved) CPC score (OR 1.28; 95% CI, 0.05 to 1.55). The direction of effect was consistent across all centers. In unresponsive survivors of OHCA, an increase in temperature control quality was associated with improved survival and better neurologic outcome; however, confounding by site, injury severity, or perceived prognosis is possible. Lack of temperature control parameter standardization may influence efficacy and practice variability within pragmatic-design clinical trials possibly contributed to neutral trial results. Prospective trials evaluating the importance of temperature control quality and the population most likely to benefit from hypothermic temperature control are essential.

articles.title: State-Level Trends in Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management Bundle (SEP-1) Compliance and Sepsis Mortality in the United States.
Frequency and Causes of Waveform Capnography Failure After Successful Emergency Tracheal Intubation.
articles.abstract: Multidisciplinary guidelines recommend waveform capnography as the preferred method for determining endotracheal tube location after intubation and advise immediate tube removal when the waveform is absent or inadequate unless a fault can be immediately identified and corrected. Because capnography depends on several components that can each fail, an absent waveform does not always indicate an esophageal tube, and removing a correctly placed tube exposes a critically ill patient to the risks of reintubation. How often waveform capnography fails despite correct tracheal placement has been estimated only from trials of colorimetric detectors in populations with high proportions of cardiac arrest, and the causes have not been described. We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected continuous quality improvement database of emergency intubations at an urban, safety-net hospital, including patients aged ≥14 years intubated between January 1, 2022, and April 21, 2025. Trained observers collected intubation data in real time, and the intubating physician completed a structured form after each procedure. The primary outcome was CO2 waveform failure following successful tracheal intubation. Secondary outcomes were the reported cause of failure and whether the tube was removed. Of 2,875 successful tracheal intubation procedures, 124 (4.3%; 95% confidence interval 3.6 to 5.1%) had CO2 waveform failure despite the tube being located in the trachea. Human error accounted for 83 events (67%), nearly all of which were from the CO2 sampling line not being connected to the bag or the monitor (82 events, 66%). Identified equipment failure accounted for 11 events (9%). The cause was undetermined in 33 events (27%), including 30 (24%) in which the failure was never explained despite confirmed tracheal placement and 3 in which the cause was not formally categorized. The endotracheal tube was removed because of the absent waveform in 1 event (1%). CO2 waveform failure occurred in approximately 4% of successful intubation procedures.

Pulmonary Function Estimation from Opportunistic Chest CT Using a Hybrid Image-plus-Quantitative-Feature Deep Learning Model.
articles.abstract: Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function. Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining? A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 80% or FVC < 80% predicted) was assessed with sensitivity, specificity and AUROC, and agreement with the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV1/FVC < 0.70; CCC 0.62) and in a low-FVC, preserved-ratio pattern (CCC 0.70-0.78). The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven. COPDGene, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT00608764.

articles.title: Antithrombin III outperforms fresh frozen plasma and improves memory recovery after severe isolated traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administered after severe isolated traumatic brain injury (TBI) has been shown to affect subsequent neurological recovery. One component of FFP, antithrombin III (AT3), demonstrates anti-inflammatory effects on the injured brain and may be a key FFP element that supports post-TBI recovery. We hypothesized that AT3 better improves cognition following severe, isolated TBI when compared with FFP. Male CD1 mice (n=29) underwent sham craniectomy (S) or craniectomy followed by severe TBI via controlled cortical impact. Mice received saline (placebo, P), FFP (10 mL/kg), or AT3 (250 IU/kg) 30 minutes after injury. Morris water maze exercises on days 6 to 14 characterized cued/spatial learning and memory. Decreased latency/distance and increased frequency/duration across four zones [zone 5 (escape platform), zone 6/zone 7 (concentric circular areas surrounding zone 5)], and zone 1 (quadrant containing zone 5) indicated superior learning and memory. The Garcia Neurological Test (GNT) allowed scoring of global animal neurological function following surgery on days 1 to 14. Mice treated with FFP or AT3 had consistent improvements in GNT scores back to sham levels across all the post-TBI experimental period from day 1 through 14 (p<0.01). Cued learning was unaffected by FFP or AT3. Spatial learning was consistently worsened by FFP but not by AT3, which, in comparison, demonstrated reduced latency to zones 5, 6, and 7 (p<0.01). FFP had no effect on memory, but AT3 consistently improved memory, decreasing latency to zones 1, 5, 6, and 7 (p<0.01) and increasing frequency into zones 1, 6, and 7 (p<0.01). There were no differences in brain or lung edema between groups. FFP after severe TBI improves global neurological recovery but appears to worsen spatial learning. Instead, AT3 confers better neurological recuperation, particularly through improved memory recovery. Further inquiry is warranted to identify beneficial and deleterious components of commonly transfused FFP to enhance recovery after severe blunt TBI.

articles.title: Bending the learning curve: Achieving faster proficiency with intrathoracic surgical stabilization of rib fractures.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is a technique for repairing the chest wall after trauma. Two primary SSRF techniques exist-intrathoracic and extrathoracic plating. This study compares our institution's proficiency acquisition and operative reference times for both techniques. A retrospective, single-institution cohort study was conducted at a level 1 trauma center to analyze the learning curves of SSRF among 12 attending surgeons who performed the extrathoracic technique and 9 who performed the intrathoracic technique from May 2015 to September 2025. Four hundred fifty-three cases were assessed, and operative times were averaged across each surgeon's cases. Plating time and exposure/closure times were reported. Cumulative sum (CUSUM) analyses with Savitzky-Golay filtering were performed to find proficiency points and operative reference times. Statistical significance was determined using parametric or nonparametric tests and multivariable linear regression. Surgeons demonstrated faster proficiency acquisition with the intrathoracic technique. When no co-surgeon was present, plating proficiency occurred after 7 cases for the intrathoracic approach and 17 cases for the extrathoracic approach. The reference time per plate was achieved at 17:03 min/plate for the intrathoracic technique and 16:56 min/plate for the extrathoracic technique. For exposure/closure times, proficiency occurred after 35 cases for the intrathoracic approach and 68 cases for the extrathoracic approach. Reference exposure/closure times were 78:57 min for the intrathoracic approach and 80:13 min for the extrathoracic approach. Intrathoracic SSRF demonstrated more rapid proficiency in both rib plating and exposure. Once proficiency has been attained, operative times are expected to align with reference times, and continued improvement towards mastery is anticipated afterwards. These findings can help establish a framework for setting expectations when onboarding new surgeons using these techniques. (J Trauma Acute Care Surg. 2026;00: 000-000. articles.title: Simultaneous clavicle and rib fracture fixation in patients with severe chest wall injuries is associated with improved outcomes: A pilot study.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Simultaneous clavicle open reduction and internal fixation (Clavicle-ORIF) with surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRFs) is an understudied but potentially beneficial strategy. We compared outcomes between patients undergoing simultaneous Clavicle-ORIF with SSRF (Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF) and those undergoing SSRF alone (SSRF-Alone) for severe chest wall injury in a pilot study to determine if there is a benefit for further research on this approach. A prospective, 2016-2025 IRB-approved database of adults undergoing SSRF at a Chest Wall Injury Collaborative Center was queried for patients with displaced clavicle fractures. Patients undergoing Clavicle-ORIF simultaneously with SSRF were compared with patients with displaced clavicle fractures for a retrospective cohort. Outcomes were daily morphine milligram equivalents, mechanical ventilation, intensive care unit days, and hospital length of stay. Of 60 consecutive patients with displaced clavicle fractures, 52 (86.7%) had complete data, of whom 17.3% underwent simultaneous Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF. The groups were similar in age (52 vs. 57 y) and injury severity (New Injury Severity Score 22 vs. 27; RibScore 4 vs. 3). Mortality was low, with 2 deaths, both in SSRF-Alone. Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF was associated with significantly fewer intensive care unit days (2 [1-3] vs. 5 [3-11], p=0.005) and less mechanical ventilation requirement (0% vs. 42%, p=0.02). Median and maximum daily morphine milligram equivalents were lower but not statistically different for Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF (38 [30-59] vs. 62 [30-83], p=0.25; and 67 [45-155] vs. 112 [61-140], p=0.61). This pilot study demonstrated that in patients with combined rib and clavicle fractures undergoing SSRF, simultaneous clavicle fixation has the potential to improve outcomes. The study was limited by a small sample size, but it justifies further research on the benefits of simultaneous clavicle fixation with SSRF. (J Trauma Acute Care Surg. 2026;00: 000-000 Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.). Pilot Retrospective Cohort; Level III.

articles.title: MPLA preconditioning protects against lethal radiation-combined burn injury with attenuation of KC/CXCL1-associated vascular leakage in mice.
articles.abstract: Radiation-combined burn injury (RCB), defined as concurrent irradiation and burn injury, is expected to be common in radiological or nuclear mass-casualty events and can be highly lethal. The mechanisms underlying the irradiation-burn interaction remain poorly understood, particularly whether it amplifies capillary leak and inflammatory mediator responses to drive early lethality. We examined whether repeated low-dose monophosphoryl lipid A (MPLA) preconditioning modulates this response and whether KC/CXCL1 contributes to vascular leakage. Male C57BL/6J mice underwent 6 Gy whole-body irradiation followed 1 h later by a 20% total body surface area full-thickness burn. MPLA (10 µg/mouse) or vehicle was administered intraperitoneally on days -4 and -3. We assessed 30-day survival, hemoconcentration, intravascular FITC-albumin retention, intestinal barrier endpoints, and cytokine/chemokine responses. A separate exploratory experiment evaluated pre-irradiation anti-KC/CXCL1 antibody treatment. Neither injury alone was lethal, whereas vehicle-treated RCB mice had 90% mortality (9 of 10 mice). Seven of these deaths occurred at 24-48 h after RCB. MPLA preconditioning increased 30-day survival from 10% to 80% ( p = 0.0003) and eliminated deaths within 48 h. RCB induced hemoconcentration and tended to reduce FITC-albumin retention. Compared with vehicle-treated RCB mice, MPLA-preconditioned RCB mice had less hemoconcentration, significantly higher FITC-albumin retention, and lower mesenteric lymph node bacterial burden. MPLA preconditioning suppressed KC/CXCL1, which showed the largest absolute increase among measured cytokines/chemokines at 6 h. Anti-KC/CXCL1 antibody treatment significantly increased FITC-albumin retention at 6 h (p = 0.038). MPLA preconditioning improved survival after RCB. It may attenuate early inflammatory and vascular abnormalities. Exploratory antibody-treatment findings suggest a possible contribution of KC/CXCL1 to early vascular albumin leakage, warranting further validation.

articles.title: [Evaluation of the practice development within advanced nursing practice in the intensive care unit].
articles.abstract: Since 2022, academically qualified nurses have been systematically integrated into direct patient care at Klinikum Oldenburg. This article describes the further development of the academic skill-grade mix, the roles of nursing experts, Advanced Practice Nurses and nursing science, and its implementation in intensive care. In 2026, an exploratory online survey assessed perceptions of the academic roles among 25 academically qualified nurses and 63 clinical staff members. Knowledge transfer, accessibility as a professional resource and practice development activities were predominantly perceived positively. At the same time, areas for further development were identified regarding role clarity and team participation. The findings suggest that sustainable implementation of academic nursing roles should be understood as an ongoing organisational development process.

articles.title: Restaurant-related occupational injuries among workers' compensation claimants in North Carolina emergency departments, 2017-2024.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Restaurant workers experience a high burden of occupational injury, particularly cuts/lacerations, burns, and slips/falls. Updated surveillance is needed to describe restaurant-related occupational injuries among workers seeking emergency care. North Carolina Disease Event Tracking and Epidemiologic Collection Tool (NC DETECT) emergency department (ED) visits from 2017 to 2024 were analyzed. Restaurant-related injuries were identified using ICD-10-CM code Y92.511 and restricted to visits listing workers' compensation as the expected payer. Annual rates per 100,000 restaurant workers were calculated. Injury characteristics were compared by sex and age using prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Overall, 654 ED visits were reported. Annual rates peaked in 2019 (36.0/100,000), declined through 2023, and increased slightly in 2024. Most injuries involved the upper extremity (59.5%) and resulted in open wounds (36.1%) or burns/corrosions (22.9%); common mechanisms included cut/pierce injuries (28.0%), contact with hot objects/substances (21.4%), and falls (20.6%). Compared with males, females had fewer open wounds (PR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.42-0.64) and cut/pierce injuries (PR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.35-0.59), but more falls (PR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.56-3.05). Compared with workers aged 15-44 years, those aged ≥45 years had more falls (PR = 3.41, 95% CI: 2.57-4.53) and fractures (PR = 3.01, 95% CI: 1.83-4.95). Restaurant-related occupational injuries commonly involved the upper extremity and were frequently associated with cuts/pierces, burns, and falls. Consistent with the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) Hierarchy of Controls, priorities could include engineering or equipment-based controls to reduce exposure to sharp instruments, hot surfaces and substances, and slipping hazards, alongside safe work practices and personal protective equipment.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing responses to treatment in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.
articles.abstract: Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities. Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment? Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m2), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) <45% predicted. A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003). PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited. In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation? and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis. When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type. In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

articles.title: Association between exertional dyspnea and insomnia in a population-based cohort.
articles.abstract: Dyspnea is unexplained in 15% of patients. Insomnia has been associated with respiratory diseases, but its relationship with dyspnea in general population remains uncertain. Is there an association between dyspnea and insomnia, defined according to different criteria, using data from a population-based cohort? Participants underwent complete respiratory, psychiatric and sleep assessments. Dyspnea (dependent variable) was defined as modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) ≥ 1. Insomnia (independent variable) was defined with Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) cut-offs ≥8 or ≥15, and with ISI categories as subthreshold (ISI 8 to 14) or clinical (ISI≥15) insomnia. Logistic regressions were performed adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, FEV1, AHI, psychiatric disorders and self-reported cardiac and respiratory disorders. We defined unexplained dyspnea with mMRC≥1 for participants of a healthy group (normal spirometry, normal Nt-proBNP, no anemia, no respiratory or cardiac disorders and normal electrocardiogram). We included 1'221 participants (mean age 62.2 years; female 52%) of whom 42% reported dyspnea and 18% reported insomnia (ISI≥8). The prevalence of dyspnea increased among ISI categories. After adjustment, higher odds of dyspnea were significantly associated with ISI cut-offs ≥ 8 (OR 1.87, CI95 1.31-2.67) and ≥ 15 (OR 1.96, CI95 1.09-3.64), as well as subthreshold insomnia (OR 1.76, CI95 1.17-2.64) and clinical insomnia (OR 2.17, CI95 1.16-4.05), all FDR p-value<0.05. Unexplained dyspnea was also associated with ISI≥8.

articles.title: Combination acetazolamide and supplemental oxygen markedly improves ventilatory control instability and OSA severity.
articles.abstract: Ventilatory control instability (elevated 'loop gain') is a key pathophysiological determinant of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but available interventions have modest potency. Since acetazolamide (ACZ) and supplemental oxygen (O2) independently lower loop gain via different mechanisms, can combination ACZO2 strongly reduce loop gain and therefore OSA severity? In a randomized, single-blind, crossover trial, 22 participants with moderate-severe OSA (15 M, 7 F), received ACZ (500 mg daily) or placebo for 7 days. On the final nights of each period, participants underwent two nights of polysomnography with O2 (3 L/min) or sham. Loop gain (LG1) and flow-based apnea-hypopnea-index (fAHI, events scored without desaturation/arousal criteria) were assessed from polysomnography at each visit. Compared with placebo+sham both ACZ and O2 monotherapies produced significant reduction in both LG1 and AHI. Combination ACZO2 markedly reduced LG1 by -0.26 [CI95%: -0.32, -0.20], and further significantly reduced LG1 compared to both ACZ (-0.07 [-0.13, -0.01]) and O2 alone -0.08 [-0.14, -0.02]. ACZO2 strongly reduced fAHI by -23.3/hr [-26.6, -13.1] (-55.2% [-63.9, -44.4]), however was not superior to ACZ alone (-3.4/h [-8.5, 1.6], -14.6% [-31.1, 5.8]). In patients with OSA, combining acetazolamide and supplemental oxygen provides a potent reduction in loop gain and roughly halves the AHI. This combination intervention holds promise for individuals whose OSA is meaningfully driven by elevated ventilatory control. ACTRN12616001297415.

articles.title: Predicting the Next Cardiac Arrest: Can the ECG Provide an Early Warning?
Establishing a Follow-up System for Survivors of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
Efficacy of Ibuprofen for the Prevention and Treatment of Acute Mountain Sickness and High-Altitude Headache: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAcute mountain sickness (AMS) and high-altitude headache (HAH) are common complications of rapid ascent to high altitude. Although acetazolamide remains the standard pharmacological prophylaxis, adverse effects may limit its tolerability. Ibuprofen has been proposed as an alternative because of its anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties. Our systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of ibuprofen for the prevention and treatment of AMS and HAH.MethodsWe searched PubMed, Science Direct, Scopus, and Web of Science for randomized controlled trials evaluating ibuprofen for the prevention or treatment of AMS or HAH. Random-effects meta-analyses were used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prevention and treatment studies and different comparators were analyzed separately. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias 2, certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) was performed for the primary AMS prevention outcome.ResultsEleven randomized controlled trials were included, of which seven contributed to at least one pooled analysis. Compared with placebo/control, ibuprofen reduced AMS incidence (6 studies; n = 739; RR = 0.61; 95% CI: 0.50-0.75) and HAH incidence (5 studies; n = 718; RR = 0.66; 95% CI: 0.44-0.99). Severe HAH was also reduced (2 studies; n = 400; RR = 0.38; 95% CI: 0.19-0.76), whereas no significant difference was observed for severe AMS, oxygen saturation, or heart rate. Compared with acetazolamide, no significant difference was observed for AMS prevention (4 studies; n = 525; RR = 0.88; 95% CI: 0.36-2.11), while the effect on HAH incidence was uncertain (3 studies; n = 432; RR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.37-1.85). Treatment trials were heterogeneous and were summarized narratively. TSA supported the benefit of ibuprofen versus placebo for AMS prevention but remained inconclusive versus acetazolamide. Certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.ConclusionsIbuprofen reduces the incidence of AMS compared with placebo and may also reduce the incidence of HAH, including severe HAH. However, evidence from active-comparator and treatment trials remains limited, and current findings do not establish equivalence with acetazolamide. Larger randomized trials are needed, particularly for treatment and direct active-comparator analyses.

articles.title: Prehospital whole blood warming and trauma-induced coagulopathy in combat casualties: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) causes significant morbidity and mortality in severely injured casualties. While low-titer group O whole blood (LTOWB) is increasingly used for prehospital resuscitation, the clinical value of active prehospital blood warming remains uncertain. We evaluated whether warmed LTOWB reduced TIC on emergency department (ED) arrival. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of combat casualties receiving prehospital LTOWB between October 27, 2023, and January 19, 2025 using linked data from the Israel Defense Forces Medical Corps Prehospital Trauma Registry and the Israeli National Trauma Registry. Patients were categorized by LTOWB administration method: active warming versus cold blood. The primary outcome was TIC on ED arrival (international normalized ratio ≥ 1.2). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between warmed LTOWB and TIC, adjusting for prehospital shock, injury severity, severe head injury, transfusion volume, and acidosis on ED arrival. Of 275 casualties receiving prehospital LTOWB, 209 were included: 61 received warmed and 148 cold LTOWB. The median age was 23 years, and most patients sustained severe or critical injuries. TIC occurred in 54 patients (25.8%), including 13 (21.3%) receiving warmed and 41 (27.7%) receiving cold LTOWB. After adjustment, warmed LTOWB was not associated with lower odds of TIC (aOR 1.07; 95% CI, 0.45-2.49). Warming was also not associated with reduced massive transfusion or improved 24-h or 30-day survival. Among combat casualties receiving prehospital LTOWB, active blood warming was not associated with reduced TIC on ED arrival. Larger studies are needed to clarify its clinical role.

articles.title: Long-Term Cognitive Function Following Haloperidol Vs. Placebo Treatment in ICU Patients With Delirium.
articles.abstract: To investigate the effects of haloperidol vs. placebo on long-term cognitive function in formerly critically ill patients with ICU delirium, 1 year after randomization in the Agents Intervening against Delirium in the ICU (AID-ICU) randomized clinical trial. Pre-planned 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU trial conducted from June 2019 to April 2023. Three university-affiliated ICUs in Denmark. Adult ICU patients previously enrolled in the AID-ICU trial. Patients in the AID-ICU were randomized to either haloperidol or placebo (0.9% saline) when treated for delirium in the ICU. The primary outcome was global cognitive function at 1 year, assessed using Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychologic Status (RBANS) Global Index Score Secondary outcomes including domain-specific RBANS scores and executive function, measured by the Trail Making Test A and B. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Non-survivors were assigned the lowest possible score on each outcome, reflecting death as a competing outcome. Missing data among survivors were handled using multiple imputations. Of the 632 randomized patients, 624 were included. Cognitive outcome data were available for 134 of 343 surviving patients: 67 in the haloperidol group and 67 in the placebo group. Median global cognitive scores were 40 (interquartile range [IQR]: 40-75) in the haloperidol group and 40 (IQR: 40-72) in the placebo group (mean difference: 2; 95% CI, -3 to 7; p = 0.48). No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. Given the high proportion of missing data, best-worst and worst-best sensitivity analyses were performed, yielding estimates in opposite directions. In this 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU treatment with haloperidol for delirium in the ICU was not associated with improved long-term cognitive function compared with placebo. However, given the extent of missing outcome data and the divergent results of our sensitivity analyses, this estimate should be interpreted as imprecise rather than conclusive; clinically relevant effects of pharmacologic delirium treatment on cognition cannot be excluded, and future adequately powered studies with more complete follow-up are warranted.

articles.title: Early serum uric acid decline and 30-day survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

Earlier Application of Methylene Blue in Vasoplegic, Adrenergic Vasopressor-Resistant Patients is Associated with Better Clinical Outcomes. A Retrospective Analysis of 464 Patients.
articles.abstract: Severe shock hails a dismal prognosis for patients in intensive care units. Vasoplegic patients, refractory to adrenergic catecholamines face an increased risk for in-hospital mortality. However, the optimal timing for Methylene Blue (MB) in these vasopressor-resistant patients, remains unclear. This was a retrospective, single-center study conducted in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a tertiary medical center. 464 patients were included, 183 (39%) admitted to the general ICU and 281 (61%) to the cardiothoracic ICU. All patients developed vasoplegia and were treated with MB after a median time of 11.2 hours from admission. In the aggregated cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with lower ICU mortality (30% vs. 52%, p < 0.001), lower in-hospital mortality (41% vs. 59%, p < 0.001), lower 1-year mortality (46% vs. 62%, p < 0.001), and reduced need for continuous Veno venous hemofiltration (33% vs. 53%, p < 0.001). In survival analyses of the whole cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with reduced in-hospital mortality in univariate analysis (HR = 0.64; 95% CI 0.47-0.86, p = 0.003) and remained significant after multivariable adjustment (HR = 0.69; 95% CI 0.51-0.94, p = 0.018). ICU-specific analyses attenuated the association. In this retrospective, single-center cohort, earlier administration of MB was associated with improved clinical outcomes among ICU patients treated for vasoplegia, including lower mortality and reduced need for renal replacement therapy. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether earlier MB administration should be incorporated into treatment protocols for adrenergic vasopressor-resistant vasoplegia.
